subject: Urgent: hardware concession & temporary burst credit request for FastHealth - proposal attached
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: FastHealth - urgent hardware concession + temporary burst credit ask (see attached)

Team — quick context: FastHealth (Asha Mendez, procurement) is at contract signature but hit two final blockers: they need H100-family GPUs for latency-sensitive inference and want a short-term burst window beyond their reservation while they ramp. Procurement pushed back on our standard overage rate and the H100 premium; they asked for an executive concession to waive the H100 surcharge for months 1–3 and provide a one-time 200k token-equivalent burst credit to smooth onboarding.

Why this matters: FastHealth is a health-tech startup moving to prod with a pilot that will scale quickly if latency targets are met. The ARR here is committed to a 36-month Dedicated reservation. Losing H100 would force them to rework model configs and slow launch by 6–8 weeks; likely churn risk.

Attachments: FastHealth_Dedicated_Order_v3.pdf (proposal with term sheet) and cost-breakdown-h100-proposal.xlsx (line-item economics).

Ask: I need an exec sign-off on two temporary exceptions:
- Waive H100 family surcharge for months 1–3 (we'd serve on H100 but price at A100-equivalent for the period)
- Approve a one-time burst credit equivalent to ~200k tokens to cover initial onboarding overages and initial peak traffic

If approved I will send a revised quote and updated order form to procurement. If we decline, Asha has indicated they will request a one-month reservation hold to evaluate alternatives.

Appreciate quick guidance — I can jump on a 15 min call.

— Priyom
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FastHealth - urgent hardware concession + temporary burst credit ask (see attached)

Thanks for the summary, Priyom. I reviewed the proposal and the economics in the spreadsheet. A couple of clarifying questions before I escalate for final sign-off:

1) Is the customer willing to lock the reservation term to 36 months with standard cancellation clauses? I want the concession tied to the committed term.
2) Does the proposed burst credit carry any usage gating (e.g., can’t be used for sustained overage beyond month 3)? We should define explicit expiration and usage constraints.
3) What fallback routing do we offer if H100 capacity is constrained? Are we committing to a hard SLA on latency or stating best-effort?

If answers look OK, I’ll put this to the deal desk exec queue and ask for a temporary H100 surcharge waiver for months 1–3 plus the one-time burst credit. Karthik — can you confirm this is within acceptable margin impact if we treat H100 as A100-priced for three months? Jordan — please prepare a redlined order form that ties the concessions to the reservation start date and expiration of the credit.

— Lauren
VP, Deal Desk
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FastHealth - urgent hardware concession + temporary burst credit ask (see attached)

Lauren — quick finance view: I ran the numbers in the attached spreadsheet (cost-breakdown-h100-proposal.xlsx). Treating H100 at A100 pricing for months 1–3 results in an expected gross margin reduction of ~4.6% across the committed term, with the one-time 200k token-equivalent credit costing us roughly $32k in gross margin. Given the strategic nature (health vertical, multi-region expansion possibility) and the size of the 36-month commit, that margin impact is acceptable.

I support the concession provided we add these guardrails:
- Concession expires automatically after month 3 and cannot be applied to renewal pricing;
- Burst credit has a hard expiration date (90 days from start) and cannot be rolled forward;
- Customer provides a signed acknowledgement accepting these constraints;
- Procurement hold triggers a narrow time-limited reservation hold (max 14 days) — if they extend beyond that we revisit pricing.

I’ll greenlight the ask for the deal desk execs to approve. Lauren — please escalate; I can join the review.

— Karthik
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Asha Mendez <asha@fasthealth.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@fasthealth.ai, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 17:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FastHealth - urgent hardware concession + temporary burst credit ask (see attached)

Thanks, Priyom — appreciate moving fast on this. We confirm the 36-month reservation and accept the guardrails Karthik proposed (expiry of concessions after 90 days, signed acknowledgement). Procurement has one small ask: can the revised order explicitly state that the one-time credit cannot be used toward reserved capacity in month 1 (we want it to cover burst usage only)? Otherwise we’re prepared to sign once we receive the updated order form.

Attachments referenced: none (we will sign electronically after receiving the updated PDF).

Best,
Asha Mendez
Director of Product Operations
FastHealth
